neighbours.label: The variable attached group in chemistry (R group, alkyl or side group, substituent): the slot that stands for whatever is attached, vs the fixed core
fire: In the textbook figure, every amino acid has an R group drawn below the central carbon.
Swapping one hydrogen for an ethyl group raised the boiling point slightly.
Bulky substituents near the double bond slow the reaction down.
The drug differs from morphine only in the side group attached to the nitrogen.
Adding a hydroxyl group to the chain makes the compound more polar.
Students compared how each substituent on the ring shifted the absorption peak.
The polymer carries a phenyl group on every second carbon.
Glycine is the simplest case because its R group is a single hydrogen.
quiet: In the textbook figure, every amino acid is drawn next to its three-letter code.
Swapping the glass flask for a steel one raised the boiling point slightly.
Bright light near the window slows the reaction down.
The drug differs from morphine only in how quickly the liver clears it.
Heating the solution gently makes the crystals dissolve more quickly.
Students compared how each sample of the dye shifted the absorption peak.
The polymer is spun into fibres and woven into rope.
Glycine is the simplest case because it is the smallest of the twenty.

predictions: 'group'/'substituent' naming a variable attached group reaches 0.4-1.2; chemistry about rings, atoms or solutions with no attached group stays under 0.15.
